Learn your TDEE, total daily energy expenditure. It factors in height, weight, sex, and activity level to give you an estimation of how much your body needs to just stay alive each day. Be honest with your activity level; if you are very overweight, your body actually requires a shit ton of food to keep all that fat warm and full of blood.

1 lb of fat = 3,500 calories. Cutting 500 calories per day = 1 lb of fat loss per week. Cutting 1,000 = 2 lbs per week. Count every calorie, use an app to make it easier.

Record everything. Sauces. Condiments. Toppings. Drinks. Coffee creamer. Cooking oil. Count that dusting of Parmesan. Count that bite of a cookie you had from the platter at work. Count that after dinner mint you had at the restaurant.

If you must drink soda, drink diet or sparkling water. You get used to it and come to appreciate having it around when you need something other than water.

Err on the side of pessimism when recording your calories. No, a small handful of broken chips is not "1 chip". It's 5. No, that wasn't 1 cup, it was 1 3/4. No, that was 4 oz not 1.5. If you want to eat fast food, go on their website for nutrition info. Set a "budget" for the meal and try to stay under it. You'd be surprised at what you can get away with eating if you just make the right choices.

If the restaurant has no calorie info, again be pessimistic when recording. Restaurants use a shitload of butter, lard, oils, etc. That's why vegetables taste amazing at the restaurant. Be careful about recorded foods in some apps; many of them are user-submitted and are flat out retarded. A burger is not 200 calories, even if you can find an entry called "burger" that's only 200 calories. It helps to record each individual component if you have access to the food packaging: bun, meat, condiments to get an accurate number.

When you start getting lower in weight things get harder. Your body has less excess fat to keep alive and so your TDEE will slowly decrease as you lose weight. Be prepared to continually cut back your food intake over time or start exercising. Bicycling is a good and fun way to exercise and is not nearly as rough as running. Weight lifting doesn't burn a high amount of calories in the moment but rather over time, as your tissue repairs and rebuilds itself. Muscle burns more calories than other tissue to keep itself alive, but unless you are seriously bulking the difference won't be that noticeable.

At the beginning of last year (after 4 months of holidays) I weighed 108kg (240 pounds). By September I was down to 76kg (167 pounds). I'm 6 foot tall so now within a healthy BMI, as before I was 'obese'. For me, this is what I did:

  • Downloaded the 'MyFitnessPal' App. Let's you track every calorie you consume.
  • Bought a small kitchen scale to weigh my food
  • Went on the Keto diet.

You'll hear a lot of people recommend / swear by keto or tell you that you're going to kill yourself - but it personally worked for me, and I have come off it now and just am very conscience of my weight so I don't slip again). Basically, it changes your metabolism to be a 'fat reliant' one - so no 'easy energy' in the form of carbohydrates (or very few anyway). If you are eating less calories than you burn (which is the main thing!) - it will fall off you. I know Reddit is a cesspool, but /r/keto is alright. My meals sorta looked like this:

Breakfast:

Eggs, Avo, Bacon, Sausage, Cheese, unflavoured yogurt

Lunch

Chicken Breast, Broccoli / salmon and poached eggs, tuna mayo salad

Dinner:

Salad, burger (no bun!), mince, stirfry

No alcohol, but if you're in a social situation and really want a drink - I had a G&T within slimline tonic water. Occasionally a JD and Diet Coke. Make sure you log all your food with the app and weigh yourself weekly - it's so easy when you're in the hang of it and serious about losing it. If you're still really hungry after a meal, down a litre of water and wait 15 minutes. If you're still hungry - nuts are great (Brazillian had the highest fat% / lowest carbs of the ones in my supermarket).

Being a very active male, I would guess around 2000 calories a day for you - probably putting you at a deficit of 1000. Just do your own research on that. There are 3500 calories in a pound of human fat - with a deficit of 1000 a day, you'll lose roughly 2-3 pounds a week. Just also make sure you are drinking 2-3 litres of water a day! Your body really needs it. I would buy a case of 12x 2l bottles of spring water from your supermarket (if they sell them in that - mine sells em 70p each) and aim to get through them in the week. Also, if you find yourself knackerd and cant be arsed cooking etc when you get home - I went and bought 14 cheap tupperware containers and would prep all my food on a Sunday afternoon while the football was on and get it out the way - so I had cheap, healthy and quick 'microwave meals' that were already preweighed.

Some quick notes too - it takes your body 2-4 days of no carbs to enter 'ketosis' (the fat reliant mode) - and sugar / complex carbs just once can throw you out of it. So if you're super wanting to cheat - just know it's cost you many days and will be 4 days again. Also, some people say they get the 'keto flu' after about a week. I didn't so don't know much about it, but look that up too - and just do as much research as you can on it. Anyway, good luck with whichever way you choose to do it - I believe you will - and hope I may have helped in some way. Take care & God bless
